name: Question 5
problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $3\times 3$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -1 \\ 10 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

Question 5
?

Which of the following matrices are transformed into the 3×3 identity matrix after applying the row operations R1:=R1+(−1)R2 and R2:=R2+(−2)R1?

A=[110411100],B=[310210001],C=[311110001]

a
A only
b
B and C only
c
A, B, and C
d
C only
e
B only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

A=[110411100]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[−30−1411100]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[−30−11013100]≠I×B=[310210001]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[100210001]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[100010001]=I✓C=[311110001]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[201110001]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[201−31−2001]≠I×

Therefore, the correct answer is "B only".
